C-CITATION-ANCHOR-REPAIR.Summary: Give every finding and decision heading in docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/decisions.md an explicit unique HTML anchor, using a delimiter-preserving slug (F9.1 → f9.1), and rewrite every internal ](#f…) / ](#d…) fragment so it resolves to exactly one of those anchors. Ship a CI check that proves uniqueness. The file does not split, move, or retire any entry. This is identity, not retirement. Links do not work under GitHub heading slugs today; this bundle makes them work for the first time.
C-CITATION-ANCHOR-REPAIR.Problem: Internal citations in docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/decisions.md are markdown fragments of the form ](#f91) and ](#d281). They follow a first-token convention that strips dots. GitHub heading slugs also strip punctuation, so F9.1 and F91 both reduce to f91, and zero current fragments match a GitHub heading id. No explicit <a id> / <a name> anchors exist. The later retirement split (registry name C-RECORD-RETIREMENT, D28 / D28.1 / F161) moves F/D bodies into other files and turns same-file fragments into cross-file references. Doing that before every heading has exactly one target leaves the colliding fragments undefined for the interval between bundles. This bundle settles identity while the file is still one document. It does not pay F161 and does not implement D28. The authority owns registry writes; this spec does not add a registry row.

Goals.Goal: Assign every heading whose text begins F<n> or D<n>, at any ATX level, exactly one explicit HTML anchor whose id is the delimiter-preserving slug of that heading.

Rewrite every ](#f…) / ](#d…) fragment in that file so it names exactly one of those ids. Mechanical where the strip-dot token matches one heading; by reading the citing sentence where it matches two or more. After apply, this is the first time those fragments resolve, not preservation of working GitHub links.

Ship scripts/validate-citation-anchors.ts on package.json validate:ci. The script exits 0 only when every F/D heading has exactly one matching anchor, ids are unique, and every f/d fragment resolves to exactly one existing id. Discriminating tests plant the refuse paths.

Constraints.Constraint: Ceremony tier T1 (module change). One markdown record file, one CI script and its test, and package.json validate:ci membership. Not T2: no skill, lint-domain, or graph-module write. Not T3: no new product subsystem.
Roadmap plan RM-GOVERNED-PATH. Identity is the precondition of D28's later split. Enforcement of uniqueness ships with the anchors, never after.

Slug grammar, delimiter-preserving. Primary slug: lowercase of the leading token matching [FD]<digits>(.<digits>)* , dots kept. F9.1 → f9.1. D28.1 → d28.1. F88.1.1 → f88.1.1. F91 → f91. Strip-dot (F9.1 → f91) is refused because it collides.

Same-token disambiguation, closed. Keep-dot does not collide distinct tokens; it still collides when two headings share the same leading token. For those headings only, the heading that is not the canonical Token — title form takes a suffix: a hyphen plus the next word after the token, lowercased (F21 correction → f21-correction; F27.1 amendment → f27.1-amendment). The heading whose first whitespace token is the id token plus 's (F19's …) takes the apostrophe-stripped first token, lowercased (f19s). The canonical Token — heading keeps the primary slug. Qualifier suffixes are not applied to unique correction/amendment headings. This is the ordinary rule that produces f21-correction; it is not a hand-assigned exception to a strip-dot grammar.

Anchor form. Immediately before each F/D heading, on its own line, an empty whose SLUG is the grammar above. id is the HTML5 fragment target. name is the custom-anchor form GitHub documents. Both attributes carry the same value. Heading text is unchanged. Pandoc / kramdown {#id} heading suffixes are refused; GitHub does not honour them.
Heading population is every ATX heading (levels 1–6) whose text begins F<n> or D<n>. A two-level cut (^### F, ^## D) is refused.

Fragment rewrite, two classes. A markdown destination matching ](#f…) or ](#d…) where the token after f/d starts with a digit, plus the existing #f21-correction, is in scope. Mechanical: the strip-dot token matches exactly one F/D heading → rewrite to that heading's keep-dot (or qualifier) slug. Reading: the strip-dot token matches two or more headings → read the citing sentence and rewrite to the intended heading's slug. #f21-correction already names the qualifier slug and stays. Non-f/d fragments (#named-bundle-registry, #slip-register--2026-08-15, and siblings) are unchanged.

The corrected fragment is the resolution record. A parallel disambiguation table is not written into this spec, the record file, or a new inventory path. Uniqueness after apply is proved by the validator. The reading of colliding citations is the git diff of those destinations.

Validator home: scripts/validate-citation-anchors.ts, invoked from package.json validate:ci (named script validate:citation-anchors running bun ./scripts/validate-citation-anchors.ts). Precedent: scripts/validate-determinism.ts and the validate:determinism member of that chain. Production invocation targets exactly docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/decisions.md. Tests live at scripts/validate-citation-anchors.test.ts and plant a missing anchor, a duplicate id, an unresolved fragment, and a happy fixture; bun test runs them via the existing test member of validate:ci. The script may take a path for those fixtures. scripts/ stays in .ngrace-lint.json ignoredDirs and is not added to the graph (M-RELEASE-AUTOMATION remains deferred). Do not add a ngrace lint issue code. Do not edit src/grace-lint.ts, src/lint/core.ts, src/lint/catalog.ts, or src/language-registry.ts CODE_EXTENSIONS.

decisions.md body text is not rewritten except (1) the inserted empty anchor lines immediately before F/D headings and (2) in-scope fragment destinations. Do not move, merge, reword, or retire any entry. Do not add, remove, or edit any finding, decision, or registry row. Do not change heading text.

AcceptanceCriteria.AC-SLUG-GRAMMAR: Every F/D heading id equals the delimiter-preserving grammar in Constraints: F9.1 is f9.1, not f91; D28.1 is d28.1, not d281; F21 correction is f21-correction; F27.1 amendment is f27.1-amendment; F19's … is f19s; the canonical F19 / F21 / F27.1 headings keep f19 / f21 / f27.1. Failure: a strip-dot id; a qualifier suffix on a unique correction heading; two headings sharing an id.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-EXPLICIT-ANCHORS: Every F/D heading at any ATX level has, on the immediately preceding line, an empty whose SLUG matches the grammar. Heading text is byte-identical to pre-change. Failure: a heading with no preceding anchor; HTML inside the heading line; a {#id} suffix; id and name disagree; a two-level cut that skips H4 findings or H3 decisions.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-FRAGMENTS-RESOLVE:
Every in-scope ](#f…) / ](#d…) fragment resolves to exactly one existing anchor id in the file. Zero of those fragments resolve under GitHub heading slugs today; after apply they resolve because of the explicit anchors, not because GitHub slugs were preserved. Failure: an unresolved fragment; two anchors for one fragment; a strip-dot destination left pointing at a keep-dot id it no longer names.
bun test scripts/validate-citation-anchors.test.ts
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-AMBIGUOUS-READ: Every fragment whose pre-change strip-dot token matched two or more headings is rewritten to the keep-dot or qualifier slug of the heading the citing sentence names. The git diff of those destinations is the reading record. Uniqueness from AC-FRAGMENTS-RESOLVE is necessary and not sufficient here. Failure: a colliding token left as strip-dot so it silently binds to the un-dotted heading; a parallel table substituted for the corrected link.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-VALIDATOR-CI:
package.json validate:ci invokes the named script validate:citation-anchors, which runs bun ./scripts/validate-citation-anchors.ts. A planted missing anchor, duplicate id, or unresolved fragment makes that script exit non-zero, and makes bun test scripts/validate-citation-anchors.test.ts fail. Failure: the script exists but is not on the chain; only bun test covers it; the check lives in ngrace lint.
bun test scripts/validate-citation-anchors.test.ts
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-NO-ARCHIVE-WRITE:
git diff against the pre-change tree has no changed path under docs/plans/archive/ or .ngrace/changes/archive/. Failure: any write there, including a fix of a stale citation.
git diff --exit-code -- docs/plans/archive/
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-DOCS-EXAMPLES:
README.md and examples/ are byte-identical to the pre-change tree.
git diff --exit-code -- README.md examples/

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Discriminating probes, not a green suite. (1) Delete one preceding <a> from a copy of the file: the validator exits non-zero. Restore: pass. (2) Duplicate an id: fail. (3) Point one fragment at a missing id: fail. (4) Leave a strip-dot destination that collides (F9.3 vs F93 both present as keep-dot ids, fragment still #f93 intending F9.3): the uniqueness check cannot catch the wrong unique target; the reading criterion is the git diff of that destination, audited against the citing sentence. (5) git diff --exit-code on docs/plans/archive, examples/, and README.md is empty. (6) Heading lines in decisions.md are unchanged except for the new preceding <a> lines and fragment destinations. Authority mutation probes on a throwaway copy; bun test green is a precondition, not the evidence.

Dot is legal in an HTML5 id (any character except space; WHATWG). Legal in HTML 4.01 ids (letters, digits, hyphens, underscores, colons, periods). Legal in a URL fragment without encoding (RFC 3986 unreserved). Legal in a CommonMark / GFM destination ](#f9.1). GitHub heading-id generation strips punctuation, so F9.1's auto id is not f9.1; that is why explicit anchors are required rather than relying on heading slugs. GitHub documents custom anchors as (docs.github.com basic writing syntax, Custom anchors). HTML5 fragment navigation uses id. CSS ID selectors must escape a dot (#f9\.1); this bundle does not style these ids. Pandoc {#id} is not GitHub GFM.
